record.paper_title: Some Open Problems in Computational Geometry
record.original_question: Given a set P of n stochastic points in R^d, where each point p in P exists independently with input probability pi(p) in (0,1], let R be the resulting random subset and let box(R) be the smallest axis-aligned box containing R. The expected volume of box(R) is known to be computable in O(n log n) time for d = 2 and in O(n^{d-1} log n) time for each fixed d >= 3, while exact computation is #P-hard when d is unbounded and d = Theta(n). Determine the parameterized complexity as a function of d: is the decision version W[1]-hard, or is it fixed-parameter tractable in d? Also find efficient approximation schemes whose dependence on d is small.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $P$ be a set of $n$ stochastic points in $\mathbb{R}^d$. Each point $p\in P$ has an associated existence probability $\pi(p)\in(0,1]$, and points exist independently of one another. Let $R\subseteq P$ be the (random) subset of points that exist, and let $\mathrm{box}(R)$ denote the smallest axis-aligned bounding box containing $R$ (with $\mathrm{box}(\emptyset)$ having volume $0$). It is known that the expected volume $\mathbb{E}[\mathrm{vol}(\mathrm{box}(R))]$ can be computed in $O(n\log n)$ time when $d=2$, and in $O(n^{d-1}\log n)$ time for each fixed $d\ge 3$; exact computation is $\#\mathrm{P}$-hard when $d$ is unbounded with $d=\Theta(n)$.

(a) Determine the parameterized complexity of computing $\mathbb{E}[\mathrm{vol}(\mathrm{box}(R))]$ (or its natural decision version) with respect to the parameter $d$: is the problem $W[1]$-hard when parameterized by $d$, or is it fixed-parameter tractable in $d$?

(b) Design an efficient approximation scheme (an FPTAS or PTAS) for $\mathbb{E}[\mathrm{vol}(\mathrm{box}(R))]$ whose dependence on the dimension $d$ is as mild as possible.
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted web search did not surface any publication resolving the parameterized complexity (in the dimension $d$) of computing the expected volume of the bounding box of a stochastic point set, nor an approximation scheme with mild dependence on $d$. The question appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: On the Parameterized Complexity of the Expected Coverage Problem
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses parameterized complexity of related expected-value stochastic geometry/coverage problems but not the stochastic bounding-box volume question.
status_evidence.claim: Related work on parameterized complexity of expected-value stochastic problems exists, but no resolution of the stochastic bounding-box problem is reported.
